detailed_findings.finding: The map Φ is well-defined: existence of minimal representatives in each nonzero residue class follows from finite complement, and positivity k_i>=1 follows from multiplicity m.
The Kunz inequalities are derived correctly from closure of S and minimality of the residue representatives, with separate cases i+j<m and i+j>m; the i+j=m case is correctly excluded.
The genus count argument is sound: in each nonzero residue class exactly the first k_i elements are missing, while all multiples of m are present.
The construction Ψ(k) is appropriate, and the closure-under-addition verification correctly uses the Kunz inequalities in the nontrivial residue-class cases.
The proof that the least positive element of Ψ(k) is m is correct because each w_i=k_i m+i exceeds m when k_i>=1.
The inverse properties Φ∘Ψ=id and Ψ∘Φ=id are established cleanly by describing elements in each residue class modulo m.
There is a minor typographical issue in one congruence display ('\pmod m}' has an extra brace), but it does not affect the mathematics.

reason: The proof correctly constructs the standard Kunz-coordinate bijection between numerical semigroups of multiplicity m and genus g and tuples satisfying the Kunz inequalities with coordinate sum g. Both directions are verified: from S to its minimal representatives w_i=k_i m+i, the inequalities and genus count are established; from k to the semigroup-like set Ψ(k), closure, finite complement, multiplicity m, and genus g are proved; and the inverse identities are checked residue class by residue class. The argument matches the semantic sketch and supports the stated cardinality equality.
